ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows an ideal operational amplifier circuit, with the non-inverting terminal grounded. The input voltage Vi is connected to the inverting input terminal through a resistor labeled 1 kΩ. Between the output terminal Vo and the inverting input node there is a feedback network: a 1 kΩ resistor and a 0.1 μF capacitor in parallel. Reasoning: This circuit is an inverting amplifier, the input resistance Rin = 1 kΩ, and the feedback impedance is Zf = Rf || 1/(jωC). Under an ideal op-amp, the inverting terminal is virtual ground, so the voltage gain magnitude is |Vo/Vi| = |Zf|/Rin. The parallel RC feedback impedance can be written as Zf = Rf/(1 + jωRfC), so the gain magnitude is (Rf/Rin)/sqrt(1 + (ωRfC)^2). From Vi = 2 sin(2π × 2000 t), the input amplitude is 2 V, the frequency f = 2000 Hz, and ω = 2πf = 2π × 2000. Substituting Rf = Rin = 1000 Ω, C = 0.1 μF = 1 × 10^-7 F, gives ωRfC = 2π × 2000 × 1000 × 1 × 10^-7 ≈ 1.2566. Therefore |gain| = 1/sqrt(1 + 1.2566^2) ≈ 0.6227. Output amplitude = 2 × 0.6227 ≈ 1.245 V, and according to the problem standard, take about 1.24 V.

method.method_draft: First identify the circuit as an inverting op-amp with R_in = 1 kΩ and feedback impedance Z_f equal to 1 kΩ in parallel with the 0.1 µF capacitor. For an ideal op-amp, the inverting input is at virtual ground, so the gain magnitude is |Z_f|/R_in = (R_f/R_in)/sqrt(1+(ωR_fC)^2). Substitute R_f = R_in = 1000 Ω, C = 0.1 µF, and ω = 2π·2000; multiply the resulting gain by 2 V to get about 1.24 V.
